plan.notes: Source: official 2026-2027 University of Colorado Boulder undergraduate catalog page 'Computer Science - Bachelor of Science (BSCS)' (College of Engineering and Applied Science), https://catalog.colorado.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/engineering-applied-science/programs-study/computer-science/computer-science-bachelor-science-bscs/. The catalog homepage confirms the current catalog is the 2026-2027 edition ('The 2026-27 University of Colorado Boulder Catalog'). Transcribed by hand on 2026-09-30 from the catalog's 'Recommended Four-Year Plan of Study' grid, cross-checked against the catalog's own program PDF (generated 2026-09-10) with layout-preserving text extraction to verify every row, credit hour, and footnote. 128 credit hours across 8 semesters (Fall Year 1 through Spring Year 4), matching the catalog's stated plan total of 128. All course codes, titles, and credit hours are verbatim from the official plan. Caveats: (1) the catalog prints 'CSCI Core course (3 of 5)' in Spring Year 3 at 4 credit hours - transcribed exactly as printed; (2) blank-label grid rows are transcribed as student-choice slots with descriptive codes (HSS Elective, Natural Science Elective, CS Core Course, CS Elective, Free Elective, Logic, Ethics, Writing Course, Natural Science Sequence, Capstone) per the plan's footnotes; footnote 1 = choose from the college-approved HSS electives list, footnote 2 = college-approved writing course, footnote 3 = CS electives per the department website; (3) CSCI 2824, CSCI 2820, and CSCI 3022 each show '(or other approved course)' in the plan - options list the catalog's approved substitutes; (4) Capstone I/II are generic 4-credit slots - the actual capstone pair is chosen from the catalog's approved two-course senior capstone sequences; (5) the catalog's requirements table totals 128-134 hours depending on options selected, while the recommended plan totals exactly 128; (6) the catalog does not publish per-slot prerequisites in the plan grid, so prereq arrays are intentionally left empty - consult the official catalog course pages and an academic advisor.
